faq_items.question: What size should I print coloring pages?
faq_items.answer: Print coloring pages at Letter size (8.5 x 11 inches), which matches standard US printer paper. Set scaling to Fit to page or 100% so the full design stays on one sheet, and nothing gets cropped at the edges or shrunk into the middle.

faq_items.question: Are these coloring pages really free to print?
faq_items.answer: Yes. Every coloring page on Biolex is a free PDF you can download and print at home with no email, no account, and no watermark. Print as many copies as you like for your own family, classroom, or a quiet evening in.

faq_items.question: What paper is best for printing coloring pages?
faq_items.answer: Plain copy paper works fine for crayons and colored pencils. If you use markers or gel pens, print on lightweight cardstock so the color does not bleed through, and the finished page feels sturdy enough to frame or give away.

faq_items.question: Why do my printed coloring pages look faded or blurry?
faq_items.answer: Faded lines usually mean your printer is set to draft or is low on black ink. Switch to Normal or High quality and check ink levels. Blurry pages often come from printing a saved web image instead of a true PDF, which holds its resolution.

faq_items.question: Can adults use these coloring pages too?
faq_items.answer: Absolutely. Intricate mandalas, florals, and repeating patterns are designed for teens and adults who want a calming, screen-free activity. The detailed line work rewards a longer sit and makes coloring a simple, low-effort way to unwind and relax.
